rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (score 933.8, best so far): oval 20/20 (mean 2.37 s, rms 0.0055), s-bend 20/20 (mean 2.53 s, rms 0.013), slalom 19/20 finished with 1 timeout and 0 off-track exits (mean progress 0.995, 0 line-loss events, min trial 429). The seven-sensor array fixed the off-track failures, so the remaining losses are the one slalom timeout and the slower completion times. The score formula rewards faster completion (60*(1-t/3)), so speed is now the main lever. Iterations 4 to 6 showed no slalom timeouts at base_speed 0.95 with the lighter body, but iteration 7 has one timeout, which points to a small speed deficit on the slalom. Change (single variable): base_speed 0.95 -> 1.0. This is about 5% more forward drive, which should cut oval and s-bend time by roughly 0.1 s and reduce slalom timeouts. Geometry, kp 4.5, kd 3.0, ki 0 and line_loss last_direction are unchanged. Expected result: slalom finish rate of 20/20 or near it, oval and s-bend still finishing with rms below 0.015, and completion_time about 2.25 s on the oval. Hypotheses to check next: (1) if slalom off-track exits return or steering_oscillation rises above 0.32, base_speed 1.0 is too fast through reversals and should return to 0.95 with a different lever such as wheel_track 0.10 m; (2) if the oval shows rms rising above 0.01, the faster speed is overshooting and kd should go up slightly; (3) if the slalom still times out at 1.0, the limit is steering authority at reversals, so narrow wheel_track to 0.10 m. Measurements requested: all metrics per track, with particular attention to slalom completion count, timeouts versus off-track exits, and completion_time on the oval and s-bend.
